title: Crypto-Assets and Other Emerging Assets
summary: How to identify, seize, hold and realise crypto-assets and other emerging asset types, working with service providers and maintaining secure custody and continuity.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: How to identify, seize, hold and realise crypto-assets and other emerging asset types, working with service providers and maintaining secure custody and continuity.
Learning Objectives: Identify indicators of crypto-asset holdings during an investigation
Explain secure seizure, custody and realisation of crypto-assets
Work with service providers to freeze and recover funds
Syllabus: Indicators of crypto-asset holdings: devices, records and statements
Seizure approaches: private keys, service providers and custody solutions
Other emerging assets: tokenised assets and online accounts
Intended Audience: Asset recovery officers, financial investigators and asset recovery office staff
Prosecutors and lawyers handling restraint, confiscation and civil recovery proceedings
Asset management office staff and customs, tax and FIU officers involved in recovering criminal proceeds
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of financial investigation, prosecution or asset recovery work is helpful. No legal qualification is required.
Core Reading: World Bank and UNODC StAR Initiative (2021), Asset Recovery Handbook: A Guide for Practitioners, Second Edition
World Bank and UNODC StAR Initiative (2009), Stolen Asset Recovery: A Good Practices Guide for Non-Conviction Based Asset Forfeiture
FATF (2012), Best Practices on Confiscation (Recommendations 4 and 38) and a Framework for Ongoing Work on Asset Recovery
UNODC (2012), Manual on International Cooperation for the Purposes of Confiscation of Proceeds of Crime
